## NET-61 — limited-memory axis, round 14 (paper 146, ResearchOutput/exp_net61_hybrid.py, /tmp/net61.log)

**Verdict name: CONTENT-ADDITIVE-EVICTION-DOES-NOT-HELP.**

### Result
Hybrid eviction score = z(accumulated usage) + λ·z(static probe score), Qwen2.5-0.5B ctx=1024 (gate exact 1.0000; probes train-side):

| B | λ | retained |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | **0.0** | **0.9384** |
| 64 | 0.25 | 0.9383 |
| 64 | 1.0 | 0.9365 |
| 64 | 4.0 | 0.9344 |
| 32 | 1.0 | 0.9189 |
| 128 | 1.0 | 0.9544 |

- **P1 REFUTED**: no λ > 0 beats λ = 0 — the response is monotonically DECREASING in probe weight.
- **P2 CONFIRMED**: λ = 0 is optimal.
- **P3 CONFIRMED**: best hybrid trails oracle@64 by 5.7 points.

Consistency anchor: the λ=0 arm reproduces NET-56's hybrid to FOUR DECIMALS (0.9384).

### The law
With NET-56 (accumulation), NET-58 (content alone), and now content-additive hybrids, every cheap eviction-signal family is bounded ≥5.7 pts below oracle at matched budget: **the policy gap is robust to accumulation, recency, content, and their linear combinations.** Remaining routes are structural (usage-tracking quality, learned online predictors at scale — themselves bounded by NET-58's weak-probe ceiling) or accepting oracle-only claims as upper bounds.

### All 8 barriers
(a) clean — three horns pre-stated incl. the refuted P1; (b) confronted — score-combination hybrids exist in H2O variants; NEW = the measured monotone-degradation law + four-family bounding of the gap; (c) confronted — one model/context, linear probes, fixed recency window; (d) clean — train-side probes; (e) deterministic, λ-grid pre-stated; (f) clean — ALL_DONE_NET61; (g) fair — identical harness/budgets/windows as NET-56/58; (h) DIRECT.

**Verdict name: THE-EPISTASIS-LIVES-IN-THE-TAIL-PAIR.**

Six pair/triple ablations at k=16/layer (Qwen2.5-0.5B, ctx=512), each cost compared to the sum of its members' NET-59 solo costs:

| arm | layers | retained | cost | Σsolo | class |

- **P3 CONFIRMED**: the tail triple compounds at 4× and is the most costly arm.

The last two layers function as a COORDINATED UNIT — co-adapted during pretraining; sparsifying either alone is absorbed, degrading both removes a joint capability no other pair exhibits. The strongest counterexample kills the tokenization hypothesis: code has 1.66× English's TPW yet needs FEWER keys; French has ~1.07× English's TPW yet needs ≥2× more keys. directions.title: Which-Factor Wall as a Cross-Population Invariant
directions.description:
Binary capacity is a strictly monotone function of class imbalance, so a wall value is a sufficient statistic for the split. We conjecture that two independent populations whose walls agree within epsilon have imbalances agreeing within C epsilon, with an explicit C controlled by the derivative of binary entropy away from 1/2.

For p, q in [delta, 1/2], |binEntropy p - binEntropy q| >= c(delta) |p - q| with c(delta) = log((1-delta)/delta), hence |p-q| <= |I_1 - I_2| / c(delta).

Differentiate binEntropy (Mathlib provides the derivative) and apply the mean value theorem on [delta, 1/2]; combine with TraceBattery.binary_wall_inversion.

The reported 0.4677 becomes a testable claim about the split (about 9.96 percent) that any replication must reproduce.

Wall values would be insensitive to imbalance near 1/2, meaning the wall carries almost no information and should be dropped from the battery report.
directions.proof_strategy: binEntropy' p = log((1-p)/p) is bounded below by log((1-delta)/delta) on the stated interval; integrate.

directions.title: Margin Scarcity as the Portability Predictor
directions.description:
Two candidate predictors of transplant damage exist in the catalog: a norm-based upper bound and a margin-based certificate. Conjecture: the margin-uncertified fraction predicts damage, and Lipschitz/norm distance between the two copies of a block does not.

Across layer blocks, the measured post-transplant disagreement correlates with the margin-uncertified fraction and is not monotone in the block's weight-space distance.

Compute both predictors per block and compare against measured disagreement, using net54_margin_failure_fraction as the certified lower bound.

Portability becomes predictable from a cheap forward-pass statistic, with no transplant needed.

Norm-based bounds remain the operative predictor and the margin route is only a sufficient condition.
directions.proof_strategy: Contrapositive of the margin transfer theorem gives the lower bound; the negative half needs an explicit pair of blocks with small norm distance and large decision divergence.

directions.description:
## NET-83 — limited-memory axis, round 33 (paper 165, ResearchOutput/exp_net83_integration.py, /tmp/net83.log)

**Verdict name: THE-INTEGRATION-IS-SUPER-ADDITIVE.**

### Result
The integration test combining GPTQ 4-bit group-128 weights with top-k attention:

| arm | retained | CE |
|---|---|---|
| full fp32 | 1.0000 | 2.697 |
| attn k=16 only | 0.9768 | 2.774 |
| attn k=20 only | 0.9803 | 2.755 |
| attn k=24 only | 0.9851 | 2.742 |
| GPTQ4 alone | 0.9081 | 3.015 |
| **GPTQ4 + k=16** | **0.8598** | **3.220** |
| **GPTQ4 + k=20** | **0.8707** | **3.180** |
| **GPTQ4 + k=24** | **0.8772** | **3.155** |

At k=16: expected additive degradation = 2.3% (attention) + 9.2% (quantization) = 11.5%. Actual combined = 14.0%. The extra 2.5% is the INTERACTION COST.

- **P1 REFUTED**: NOT sub-additive
- **P2 CONFIRMED**: super-additive — sparse attention AMPLIFIES quantization noise
- **P3 REFUTED**: the axes are NOT independent

### Mechanism
(1) Quantized key vectors project differently, changing which keys pass the top-k threshold.
(2) Selected keys' values carry quantization error that the sparse weighted sum cannot average away.

### Engineering consequence
Budget tables must include an INTERACTION PENALTY when both optimizations are active. A 4-bit model with k=24 attention is NOT equivalent to a 4-bit model plus a 24-key cache.

### Debug transparency
SEVEN debug iterations before recording; SIX bugs caught by sanity gates including a critical runner-layers reference bug that silently evaluated the wrong model.
